panels.title: Leaving Earth orbit
body: At ground elapsed time 2:50:03.2 (16:22:03 UTC, 16 July 1969) the S-IVB's second burn cut off. NASA's postflight table puts the stack about 321 km above Earth, moving at about 10.84 km/s relative to Earth's centre.
The next anchor, translunar injection, follows ten seconds later.
sources: NASA Apollo 11 Mission Report (MSC-00171), Table 7-II, p. 7-9: anchor A-02, S-IVB second cutoff

panels.title: Touchdown at Landing Site 2
body: Eagle touched down at ground elapsed time 102:45:39.9 (20:17:40 UTC, 20 July 1969), at 0.674° N, 23.473° E on the Moon.
The touchdown time and place are published values. The descent path drawn to reach them is a reconstruction: powered descent is a two-anchor interpolation, not a measured track.
sources: NASA Apollo 11 Mission Report (MSC-00171), Table 5-IV, p. 5-10: anchor A-LND, lunar touchdown (Landing Site 2)
Astraeus Apollo 11 reconstruction notes: powered descent and ascent remain two-anchor interpolations
